active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.savgol_filter with optimized boundary handling
active_paradigms.description: Replace the current multi-stage SG+Kalman+smoothing pipeline with a single scipy.signal.savgol_filter call. This compiled C implementation is more numerically stable than manual polyfit. Use window_length=19 (matching evaluator delay) and polyorder=2 for quadratic fitting. Set boundary='extend' to improve edge handling and reduce false reversals at signal boundaries. The single-stage approach eliminates cumulative lag from cascaded filters while maintaining polynomial fitting benefits. This directly addresses the lag error (L_recent) by removing the exponential smoothing stage that adds unnecessary delay.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce lag error (L_recent) by eliminating multi-stage lag; reduce false reversals (R) with better edge handling; improve slope changes (S) through consistent polynomial fitting
active_paradigms.cautions: Window_length must be odd and less than signal length; test polyorder=2,3,4 for optimal smoothness vs tracking; ensure boundary mode doesn't introduce artifacts at edges

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.wiener for adaptive noise reduction
active_paradigms.description: Apply scipy.signal.wiener filter which adaptively estimates local mean and variance in a sliding window, then applies optimal Wiener filtering based on local signal-to-noise ratio. This is fundamentally different from polynomial fitting - it's designed specifically for noise reduction while preserving signal dynamics. Use mysize=20 to match the evaluator's window size. The filter automatically adapts to different signal types (sinusoidal, step, random walk) without parameter tuning, providing robust performance across all test signals. Wiener filtering is optimal for Gaussian noise and provides better tracking accuracy than fixed-parameter approaches.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve tracking accuracy (L_avg) and reduce lag error (L_recent) through adaptive noise estimation; maintain good performance across diverse signal types without parameter tuning; reduce false reversals (R) by adapting to local signal characteristics
active_paradigms.cautions: Wiener filter assumes stationary noise within window; may need to adjust mysize for different signal frequencies; test with varying noise levels to ensure robustness across all 5 test signals

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.butter + scipy.signal.lfilter for custom low-pass filtering
active_paradigms.description: Design a Butterworth low-pass filter using scipy.signal.butter with order=4 and normalized cutoff frequency=0.1 (10% of Nyquist). Apply with scipy.signal.lfilter for single-stage IIR filtering. Butterworth provides maximally flat frequency response in passband, preserving signal dynamics while reducing noise. This deterministic setup (butter) followed by single filtering call (lfilter) replaces the multi-stage pipeline. The filter order and cutoff can be tuned to balance smoothness vs tracking accuracy. Unlike the current Kalman approach, this provides consistent frequency-domain behavior across all signal types.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) through controlled frequency response; maintain low lag error (L_recent) with appropriate cutoff frequency selection; improve tracking accuracy (L_avg) with maximally flat passband
active_paradigms.cautions: Cutoff frequency must be chosen carefully - too low loses signal dynamics, too high leaves noise; filter order affects phase response; test different cutoff values (0.05-0.2) for optimal performance across signal types

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.stats.kde and Kalman Filter for adaptive state-space filtering
tried_paradigms.description: Implement a Kalman filter using numpy matrix operations to model the signal as a state-space system with position and velocity states. The Kalman filter naturally minimizes lag through velocity prediction while adaptively adjusting to signal volatility. Calculate measurement noise variance from recent signal differences using rolling statistics, and tune process noise to balance smoothness vs responsiveness. The filter produces optimal estimates that minimize both lag error and false reversals by properly modeling the underlying signal dynamics. Unlike the current momentum hysteresis approach, the Kalman filter provides mathematically optimal state estimation with minimal tuning required.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce false reversals (R) and lag error (L_recent, L_avg) while maintaining tracking accuracy through optimal state estimation
tried_paradigms.cautions: Ensure matrix operations are stable, initialize state covariance properly, tune process noise variance to avoid over-smoothing or excessive lag

tried_paradigms.idea: Use pywt wavelet denoising with sym5 wavelet for multi-scale noise reduction
tried_paradigms.description: Apply wavelet transform using pywt.wavedec with sym5 wavelet at decomposition level 3 to separate signal from noise across frequency scales. Use soft thresholding on detail coefficients to remove high-frequency noise while preserving signal dynamics and genuine trend changes. Reconstruct the signal with pywt.waverec, which naturally handles non-stationary signals better than polynomial fitting. Wavelet denoising excels at preserving sharp transitions (reducing false reversals) while removing noise (reducing slope changes). This fundamentally different approach works in the frequency domain rather than time domain.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Minimize slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) by removing high-frequency noise while preserving genuine signal dynamics across multiple scales
tried_paradigms.cautions: Choose appropriate wavelet family and decomposition level, use soft thresholding to avoid ringing artifacts, ensure output length matches input

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.medfilt with volatility-adaptive trend confirmation
tried_paradigms.description: Apply median filtering using scipy.signal.medfilt with window size 9 to robustly remove outliers and spurious noise spikes. Then implement a simple trend confirmation mechanism that only updates the output when signal changes exceed a volatility-adaptive threshold (e.g., 0.5 * rolling std). This two-step approach is simpler than momentum hysteresis but achieves similar false reversal reduction. Median filtering is inherently robust to outliers and produces fewer spurious slope changes. The adaptive threshold ensures genuine trend changes are captured while noise-induced reversals are filtered out.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) through robust outlier rejection and simple trend confirmation
tried_paradigms.cautions: Median filter adds slight lag, ensure adaptive threshold doesn't miss genuine trend changes, handle edge cases with small windows

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.medfilt for robust outlier rejection before Kalman filtering
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the Savitzky-Golay filter with scipy.signal.medfilt for initial noise reduction. Median filtering is robust to outliers and preserves edges better than polynomial fitting, which helps reduce false reversals (R metric). After median filtering, apply the Kalman filter directly without the lag-inducing exponential smoothing layer. This creates a simpler two-stage pipeline: medfilt removes impulsive noise while preserving signal transitions, then the Kalman filter with velocity prediction provides optimal state estimation. The median filter's edge-preserving property directly addresses the slope change penalty (S) by not creating artificial reversals at noise peaks.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversal penalty (R) and slope changes (S) by using edge-preserving median filter; maintain lag performance through Kalman prediction
tried_paradigms.cautions: Choose appropriate median filter window size (odd numbers only, typically 3-7); ensure output length matches input for proper alignment with evaluator's delay calculation; remove the light_smooth exponential smoothing layer that adds lag

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.wiener for adaptive noise reduction with local statistics estimation
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the entire multi-stage pipeline with scipy.signal.wiener filter, which adaptively estimates local noise statistics and applies optimal Wiener filtering in each window. The Wiener filter minimizes mean square error between filtered and original signals, directly optimizing the L_avg metric. It automatically adapts to local signal characteristics without needing manual parameter tuning for different signal types. This single-function approach eliminates the length mismatch issues between Savitzky-Golay (which outputs n-window+1 samples) and Kalman filter (which expects full length). The adaptive nature handles both smooth sinusoidal signals and step changes equally well.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Average tracking error (L_avg) and correlation with clean signal through optimal MSE minimization; improve consistency across different signal types
tried_paradigms.cautions: Wiener filter uses a default 3x3 window for 1D signals; may need to test different window sizes; ensure filtered output length matches input for proper evaluator alignment; this is a single-stage filter so no length mismatch issues

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.savgol_filter with forward extrapolation and remove post-smoothing
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the custom Savitzky-Golay implementation with scipy.signal.savgol_filter, which is more optimized and includes built-in boundary handling options. Use the 'interp' mode or pad the signal appropriately to maintain full output length. Critically, remove the light_smooth exponential smoothing layer entirely as it adds lag without significant benefit. The scipy implementation handles edge cases better and can use polynomial extrapolation at boundaries. Additionally, increase the Kalman filter's process noise parameter to make it more responsive to genuine signal changes, reducing the false reversal penalty when clean signal has trend changes.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent) by removing post-smoothing layer; improve slope changes (S) through better boundary handling; maintain tracking accuracy through proper length alignment
tried_paradigms.cautions: scipy.signal.savgol_filter with mode='interp' or proper padding is needed to maintain full length; polynomial order should be even (2 or 4); window size must be odd; ensure the filtered signal length matches the input for proper delay calculation in evaluator
